title: Cranberry Whipped Cream
description: Sweet cranberry purée whipped into cream: blush pink and made for eating with a spoon or scooping with cookies.

items.note: about 6 oz; no need to thaw

steps.text: Combine {cranberries}, {sugar}, {water}, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan over medium heat. Simmer, stirring and pressing the berries against the pan, until they've all burst and the mixture is thick and jammy, 8 to 10 minutes.
steps.why: Cooking it down to jam drives off water. Every bit of liquid left in the purée is liquid the cream has to carry, and a thin purée deflates whipped cream.

steps.text: Let the cranberries cool for 10 minutes until warm, not hot, then blend until completely smooth.
steps.why: Never blend hot fruit in a sealed blender: steam builds pressure and can blow the lid off. Blending instead of straining keeps the skins, which add body and deepen the pink.

steps.text: Chill the purée completely, at least 1 hour in the fridge, or spread it thin on a plate and freeze 15 minutes.
steps.why: Warm purée melts the fat in cold cream, and melted fat won't hold air. It must be fully cold before it meets the cream.

steps.text: Chill the mixing bowl and beaters or whisk in the freezer for 10 minutes before whipping.
steps.why: Cold equipment keeps the cream's fat firm, which is what traps the air. A warm bowl means slower whipping and a softer result.

steps.text: Whip {cream}, {powdered-sugar}, and {vanilla} to soft peaks: the cream holds a shape that slumps over at the tip.
steps.why: Powdered sugar dissolves instantly in cold cream, and its cornstarch helps the cream hold its shape once the tart purée goes in.

steps.text: Add the cold cranberry purée and whip just until medium peaks form and the color is even blush pink. Stop the moment the tips stand up and curl slightly.
steps.why: Cranberry's acid tightens cream fast, so it goes from soft to stiff in seconds. Overwhipped cream turns grainy and starts heading toward butter.

steps.text: Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate. Give it a few gentle strokes with a whisk before serving if it has loosened.

notes.title: Make-ahead
notes.body: The purée keeps 5 days refrigerated, so make it ahead and whip the cream the day you serve. The finished whipped cream holds 1 to 2 days covered in the fridge.

notes.title: Sweetness
notes.body: Taste the cream after the purée goes in. If you want it sweeter still, whip in more powdered sugar a spoonful at a time: it dissolves without any grit.

notes.title: If it goes grainy
notes.body: Overwhipped cream can be rescued: gently whisk in a splash of cold heavy cream by hand until it smooths out again.

plating: Pile it into small glasses or bowls and eat it with a spoon, or set out a plate of cookies for scooping.
elevations: A spoonful of freeze-dried cranberry powder for deeper color and flavor without adding any liquid.
White chocolate shaved over the top.
Layer it in glasses with crushed cookies for a quick parfait.

changelog.note: Sweeter, built to eat on its own or with cookies. Orange removed. Cranberries are blended instead of sieved, the way Cody made it.
